## Historical audit — S0162, chunk 1 of 3

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/r1/sceneevolve_cli/C2/development/commons_109923183/trajectory.jsonl`. Citations below refer to its JSONL lines. The other chunks and image pixels are not available to this audit.

| Evidence | Observed operation or result |
|---|---|
| Student request, line 1 | Goal: reconstruct an indoor photograph as editable multipart SceneAct/Blender geometry, matching viewpoint, framing, colors and occlusions without using the reference as a texture. |
| Student response, line 3; execute, line 4 | The student described a chaise, pillow, cropped cane chair, paneled room and curtains, then supplied a complete program with separate assemblies. It positioned and rotated furniture and pillow, constructed legs, rails and upholstery, and specified procedural fabric and floor shaders, camera and lights. Assembly membership and intended adjacency are evidenced; actual geometric connection is not independently checked. |
| Execution result, line 5 [0,61943); select events, lines 6–7 | Step 1 reports `ok: true`, a completed render and saved image and scene. Selection of step 1 is recorded. This is **technical execution success**, not proof of visual or geometric fidelity. |
| Student audit, line 10 | After the reference and render were supplied in the next request (line 8), the student estimated that framing was too wide, the pillow/head too narrow, the under-seat opening too large, the wall boundary too low and surfaces too bright. These are student visual judgments, not independent measurements. It proposed a 60 mm lens, pillow/wing/apron changes, simpler moldings and darker materials, with wall movement conditional on the lens result. |
| Student response, line 14; execute, line 16 | The complete step-2 program adopted those self-proposals: lens 47→60 mm, widened and rotated pillow, deeper wing, solid apron sections, fewer moldings and darker floor/frame. It moved the wall by 0.25 m without a separately visible post-lens-only test. Light powers remained fixed. |
| Execution result, line 17 [0,62814); select events, lines 18–19 | Step 2 also reports `ok: true` and a saved render. Selection events record step 2, then step 1. Their ultimate submission meaning and any later evaluation are unknown in this chunk. |

**Input and exploration.** The visible critique was the student’s own, prompted by the runner; no teacher feedback, teacher detection, diagnosis or proposed update is visible, so teacher receipt or adoption cannot be established. The student autonomously produced an initial specification and program, then audited a supplied render and revised it. The recorded student CLI sessions show no tool calls (lines 2, 9 and 13); the external runner performed the executions.

**Assessment and uncertainty.** Multiple modeled objects, distinct materials, pose parameters and camera/light settings are evidenced by code, not by independently inspected images. The student identified possible framing, material and geometry issues; whether either render matches the photograph, whether parts visibly intersect or connect properly, and whether step 2 improves step 1 remain unresolved. No technical interruption, empty patch, or algorithm failure is shown; overall formal success or partial correctness is unknown.

**Lessons.** Transferably, distinguish render completion from scene accuracy and separate framing, local geometry and brightness hypotheses before testing. Task-specific hypotheses here concern the chaise opening, pillow orientation and wall boundary; the combined step-2 changes do not isolate their individual effects.
